facts.statement: Ekrixinatosaurus is a genus of abelisaurid theropod that lived during the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Ekrixinatosaurus ('explosion-born reptile') is a genus of abelisaurid theropod which lived during the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Only one species of Ekrixinatosaurus is currently recognized: Ekrixinatosaurus novasi.
facts.quote: Only one species is currently recognized, Ekrixinatosaurus novasi

facts.statement: Ekrixinatosaurus novasi was first described in 2004 by Jorge Calvo, David Rubilar-Rogers, and Karen Moreno.
facts.quote: The type species, Ekrixinatosaurus novasi, was first described in 2004 by Argentinian paleontologist Jorge Calvo, and Chilean paleontologists David Rubilar-Rogers and Karen Moreno.

facts.statement: The discovery of Ekrixinatosaurus occurred during excavations for a gas pipeline in Bajo del Añelo.
facts.quote: The discovery occurred due to excavations for building a gas pipeline conducted by Gasoducto del Pacífico Company in Bajo del Añelo.

facts.statement: The age of the Candeleros Formation, where Ekrixinatosaurus fossils were found, was re-dated to the early Albian, approximately 111.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Originally suggested to be the Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous, the maximum depositional age of both the Candeleros Formation and the overlying Huincul Formation is re-dated to the early Albian by Maniel et al. (2026), approximately 111.4 ± 1.1 Ma and 106.2 ± 1.0 Ma respectively.

facts.statement: Ekrixinatosaurus had a large skull, prominent supraorbital ridge, compressed neck vertebrae, and robust short hindlimbs, suggesting it was built to sustain injuries during combat.
facts.quote: The combination of characteristics including a large skull, prominent supraorbital ridge above the dorsal aspect of the orbit, anteroposteriorly compressed cervical vertebrae, and robust, proportionally short hindlimbs with a tibia shorter than femur suggests that this was a massive animal with a great capacity to sustain injuries during intraspecific or interspecific combat.

facts.statement: The maxilla of Ekrixinatosaurus was short and contained 16 tooth sockets with teeth that were flattened laterally and had serrations on both front and back edges.
facts.quote: The maxilla was short and contained 16 alveoli, some with short teeth that were flattened laterally with anterior and posterior serrations.

facts.statement: In 2004, Ekrixinatosaurus was classified within the family Abelisauridae.
facts.quote: In 2004, Ekrixinatosaurus was placed in the Abelisauridae by Calvo and colleagues.

facts.statement: Ekrixinatosaurus lived in the red beds of the Candeleros Formation, an environment that supported a wide variety of vertebrates.
facts.quote: Ekrixinatosaurus was found in the red beds of the Candeleros Formation, which has yielded a wide variety of vertebrates.

facts.statement: Ekrixinatosaurus shared its habitat with sauropods such as Andesaurus, Limaysaurus, and Nopcsaspondylus.
facts.quote: It shared its environment with the titanosaurian sauropod Andesaurus and the rebbachisaurid sauropods Limaysaurus and Nopcsaspondylus.

facts.statement: Giganotosaurus was possibly the apex predator in the same ecosystem as Ekrixinatosaurus.
facts.quote: The carcharodontosaurid Giganotosaurus was possibly the apex predator.

facts.statement: It is debated whether abelisaurids like Ekrixinatosaurus only became top predators after carcharodontosaurids went extinct.
facts.quote: It has been hypothesized that it was only after extinction of these carcharodontosaurids that abelisaurids were able to diversify into more robust forms that occupied the niche of top predators of their ecosystems.

facts.statement: The coexistence of large Giganotosaurus and Ekrixinatosaurus refutes the hypothesis that abelisaurids only became top predators after carcharodontosaurid extinction.
facts.quote: However, it has been observed that both Giganotosaurus and Ekrixinatosaurus were among the largest of their respective clades yet existed at the same time, which refutes this hypothesis.

facts.statement: Early size estimates suggested Ekrixinatosaurus reached 6 to 8 meters in length with a head measuring 830 millimeters.
facts.quote: Los cálculos iniciales de su tamaño indicaron que llegó a medir entre 6 a 8 metros de largo con una cabeza de 830 milímetros.

facts.statement: Other estimates proposed it was likely the largest abelisaurid, measuring between 10 to 11 meters long.
facts.quote: Otras estimaciones indicaron que probablemente es el mayor de los abelisáuridos, midiendo entre 10 a 11 metros de largo.

facts.statement: A 2016 study revised the size down to approximately 7.40 meters, noting it was smaller than Carnotaurus at 7.80 meters.
facts.quote: Más tarde, un estudio de 2016 de nuevo halló que era más pequeño, unos 7,40 metros, menos que Carnotaurus de 7,80 metros.

facts.statement: Its head was relatively larger than in Carnotaurus, with an extrapolated skull-to-femur ratio of 1.00 compared to 0.58.
facts.quote: Su cabeza es relativamente más grande que en Carnotaurus, con un cociente extrapolado de 1,00 entre el cráneo y el fémur comparado a 0,58

facts.statement: The skull possessed a window between the postorbital and frontal bones and a posteriorly directed protuberance contacting the parietal and paroccipital processes.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Ekrixinatosaurus posee una ventana entre el postorbital y el frontal, una protuberancia dirigida posteriormente en contacto del proceso parietal y paroccipital.

facts.statement: Its cervical vertebrae were anteroposteriorly compressed with dorsal neural spines as high as the epipophyses.
facts.quote: Sus vértebras cervicales anteroposteriormente comprimidas, con las espinas vértebrales dorsales tan altas como epipofisis.

facts.statement: The middle to posterior cervical centra had a flat ventral surface and two wide holes in the middle and posterior cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: Los centros cervicales medio posteriores con vientre plano y dos agujeros anchos en las vértebras cervicales medias y posteriores.

facts.statement: The tibia featured a widening in its middle section.
facts.quote: La tibia poseía un ensanchamiento en la parte media.

facts.statement: The skull was square and proportionally shorter and deeper than most other large carnivorous dinosaurs.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Ekrixinatosaurus era cuadrado y proporcionalmente más corto y más profundo que la mayoría de los otros dinosaurios carnívoros grandes.

facts.statement: The jaws curved upward, a trait shared with some other abelisaurids.
facts.quote: Las mandíbulas también se curvaron hacia arriba, un rasgo compartido con algunos otros abelisáuridos.

facts.statement: The skull is estimated to be approximately 83 centimeters long based on comparisons with Carnotaurus and Majungasaurus.
facts.quote: El cráneo se estima en aproximadamente 83 centímetros de largo según las comparaciones con Carnotaurus y Majungasaurus

facts.statement: The short upper jaw contained 16 alveoli, some with short teeth that flattened laterally with anterior and posterior striations.
facts.quote: El maxilar era corto y contenía 16 alvéolos, algunos con dientes cortos que se aplanaban lateralmente con estrías anteriores y posteriores.

facts.statement: The upper jaw exhibited a dorsally projecting ascending ramus and a short rostral ramus, suggesting a relatively high skull.
facts.quote: El maxilar superior de Ekrixinatosaurus también exhibe una rama ascendente dorsalmente proyectada y una rama rostral corta, lo que sugiere un cráneo relativamente alto.

facts.statement: Remains were found in the Candeleros Formation of the Río Limay Group in northwestern Neuquén Province, Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Los restos se encontraron en la Formación Candeleros del Grupo Río Limay, en al noroeste de la Provincia del Neuquén, Patagonia Argentina.

facts.statement: The holotype MUCPv-294 was a well-preserved disarticulated skeleton including the left maxilla and parts of the right, skull base, dentaries, teeth, cervical, dorsal, sacral, and caudal vertebrae, hemal arches, ribs, ilium, pubis, proximal ischium, left femur and distal right femur, left tibia, astragalus and calcaneus, proximal left fibula and right tibia, metatarsals, phalanges, and a pedal ungual.
facts.quote: El holotipo MUCPv-294 un bien preservado esqueleto desarticulado que incluía el maxilar izquierdo y partes del derecho, la base del cráneo, ambos dentarios, dientes, vértebras cervicales, dorsales, sacras y caudales, arcos hemales, costillas, ilion, un pubis y la parte proximal del isquion, fémur izquierdo y extremo distal del derecho, tibia izquierda, astrágalo y calcáneo izquierdo, un extremo proximal del peroné izquierdo y de la tibia derecha, metatarsos, falanges y un ungular pedal.

facts.statement: The type species, Ekrixinatosaurus novasi, was first described in 2004 by Argentine paleontologist Jorge Calvo and Chilean paleontologists David Rubilar-Rogers and Karen Moreno.
facts.quote: La especie tipo , Ekrixinatosaurus novasi, fue descrita por primera vez en 2004 por el paleontólogo argentino Jorge Calvo y los paleontólogos chilenos David Rubilar-Rogers y Karen Moreno.

facts.statement: The discovery occurred during excavations for a gas pipeline built by the Compañía Gasoducto del Pacífico at Bajo del Añelo.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento ocurrió debido a las excavaciones para construir un gasoducto conducido por la Compañía Gasoducto del Pacífico en Bajo del Añelo.

facts.statement: The fossils were found scattered over an area of 15 square meters in the Candeleros Formation.
facts.quote: Los fósiles se encontraron dispersos en un área de 15 m² en la Formación Candeleros

facts.statement: The Candeleros Formation dates to 100 to 97 million years ago.
facts.quote: Esta formación data de 100-97 millones de años atrás

facts.statement: The name derives from the fact that fossils were found after an explosion during a mining operation.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de este dinosaurio se encontraron luego de una explosión realizada en una operación minera, de allí viene su nombre.

facts.statement: The generic name combines the Greek word Ekrixi meaning 'explosion' with the Latin nato meaning 'born' and the Greek suffix saurus meaning 'lizard'.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico proviene de la combinación de la palabra en griego Εκρηξι, Ekrixi que significa "explosión" con el término en latín nato por nacimiento y la terminación griega usual saurus que se traduce como lagarto.

facts.statement: The species E. novasi was named in recognition of Fernando Novas.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, E. novasi descrita por los paleontólogos Jorge Calvo de Argentina y David Rubilar-Rogers y Karen Moreno de Chile en 2004, fue nombrada en reconocimiento a Fernando Novas.

facts.statement: A preliminary cladistic analysis places Ekrixinatosaurus with Majungatholus and Carnotaurini as a sister group to Ilokelesia.
facts.quote: Un análisis cladístico preliminar coloca a Ekrixinatosaurus, descubierto en 1999, junto con Majungatholus y Carnotaurini y hermano de grupo con Ilokelesia.

facts.statement: Its presence in sediments ranging from the Albian to Cenomanian supports a theory of early divergence of abelisaurids prior to the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: La presencia de este espécimen en sedimentos que oscilan entre el Albiense y el Cenomaniano apoya la teoría de una divergencia temprana, previa al Senoniano de los abelisáuridos

facts.statement: Ekrixinatosaurus lived approximately 100 to 97 million years ago.
facts.quote: Esta formación data de 100-97 millones de años atrás

facts.statement: It inhabited the red beds of the Candeleros Formation, which yielded a wide variety of vertebrates.
facts.quote: Ekrixinatosaurus se encontró en los lechos rojos de la formación Candeleros, que ha dado lugar a una amplia variedad de vertebrados.

facts.statement: It shared its environment with the titanosaurian sauropod Andesaurus and the rebbachisaurid sauropods Limaysaurus and Nopcsaspondylus.
facts.quote: Compartió su entorno con el titanosauriano saurópodo Andesaurus y los rebaquisáurido saurópodos Limaysaurus y Nopcsaspondylus.

facts.statement: The carnosaur Giganotosaurus was possibly the apex predator in the ecosystem.
facts.quote: El carcarodontosáurido Giganotosaurus fue posiblemente el depredadorapice.

facts.statement: Smaller predators also inhabited the area, including the dromaeosaurid Buitreraptor, the alvarezsaurid Alnashetri, and the basal ceratosaurian Bicentenaria.
facts.quote: Los depredadores más pequeños también habitaban el área, incluido el dromeosáurido Buitreraptor, el alvarezsáurido Alnashetri y el celurosaurio basal Bicentenaria.

facts.statement: A wide variety of dinosaur tracks found in the Candeleros Formation suggests significant activity in the area.
facts.quote: También se ha encontrado una amplia variedad de vías de dinosaurios en la Formación Candeleros , lo que sugiere una actividad significativa en el área.

facts.statement: It is debated whether abelisauroids only diversified into robust forms occupying the top predator niche after the extinction of giant carnosaurids.
facts.quote: Se ha planteado la hipótesis de que solo después de la extinción de estos carcarodontosáuridos los abelisauroides pudieron diversificarse en formas más robustas que ocuparon el nicho de los principales depredadores de sus ecosistemas.

facts.statement: However, the observation that both Giganotosaurus and Ekrixinatosaurus were among the largest in their respective clads but coexisted refutes the hypothesis that abelisauroids only became dominant after carnosaur extinction.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, se ha observado que tanto Giganotosaurus como Ekrixinatosaurus se encontraban entre los más grandes de sus respectivos clados, pero existían al mismo tiempo, lo que refuta esta hipótesis.

facts.statement: It is unknown whether they played different ecological roles, such as active predation versus scavenging.
facts.quote: no se sabe si jugaron diferentes roles ecológicos, como la depredación activa contra carroñeo.

facts.statement: The fossil record indicates a time range from 113.2 to 110.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 110.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is classified within the family Abelisauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Abelisauridae

facts.statement: It belongs to the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
